related_questions.question: How long do you feel unwell after a COVID shot?

text_blocks.snippet: Most people who experience side effects from the COVID-19 vaccine feel unwell for a few days, typically within the first 24-48 hours after vaccination. These side effects are usually mild, like pain or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, or flu-like symptoms. They tend to resolve on their own within a few days. If side effects are severe or persist longer than a few days, it's recommended to seek medical advice.
snippet_highlighted_words: typically within the first 24-48 hours after vaccination

list.title: Onset:
list.snippet: Side effects typically begin within the first 24 hours after vaccination.

list.title: Duration:
list.snippet: Most side effects are short-lived, usually resolving within 24-48 hours, but some might last for a few days.

list.title: Severity:
list.snippet: Side effects are generally mild, like pain or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, chills, or fever, according to the CDC.

list.title: Severe reactions:
list.snippet: While rare, severe allergic reactions can occur, requiring immediate medical attention. Symptoms include difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, dizziness, and a rapid heartbeat.

list.title: Seeking help:
list.snippet: If side effects are severe or don't improve within a few days, it's important to contact a healthcare provider.

related_questions.question: What are the side effects of the new COVID shot?

text_blocks.snippet: Common side effects of the new COVID-19 shots are similar to those of previous ones, including pain or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, chills, fever, and nausea. These side effects are generally mild and temporary, typically lasting 1-2 days. More serious side effects like myocarditis are rare.
snippet_highlighted_words: pain or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, chills, fever, and nausea

list.snippet: Injection Site Reactions: Pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site.
Systemic Reactions: Fatigue, headache, muscle pain, chills, fever, and nausea.
Over-the-counter pain relievers: Medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help relieve pain and fever.
Rest: Getting plenty of rest can help your body recover.
Hydration: Drinking plenty of fluids is important, especially if you have a fever.
Cool compresses: Applying a cool, damp cloth to the injection site can help reduce swelling and pain.
Myocarditis: Inflammation of the heart muscle, particularly in young men. This is a rare side effect, but some studies have reported its occurrence, especially after mRNA vaccines.
Pericarditis: Inflammation of the lining of the heart.

list.title: Consult your doctor:
list.snippet: If you have any concerns about side effects or if they persist or worsen, consult your doctor.
